title: TICON-3: tidal constants of 3,471 tide gauges from GESLA-3 sea-level records (amplitude and Greenwich phase lag of 40 constituents)

radius_enters_via.field: frequencies and equilibrium arguments of the constituents
radius_enters_via.how: not the radius: each gauge's constants were fitted with the frequencies of the Moon's and Sun's motions; the page predicts the tide from them with the same arguments

verdict_rule: Gauges whose constants show no twice-daily line at the Moon's frequency along a whole coast, or tides in small closed seas as large as on the open ocean, would favour a local Moon lifting water under itself.

sources.cite: M. G. Hart-Davis, D. Dettmering, F. Seitz, TICON-3: Tidal Constants based on GESLA-3 sea-level records from globally distributed tide gauges including gauge type information (data), PANGAEA (2022), doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.951610

units.phase lag: deg, Greenwich lag, 0-360 (Foreman's convention: diurnal constituents carry a quarter-cycle constant)

inputs.checks: Rows with one number missing (four Great Lakes stations) are skipped and counted.

notes: Four NOAA stations of the Great Lakes have rows with only one of the five numbers after the constituent name; they are skipped and counted. The gauge type 'Lake' also covers tidal lagoons and estuaries (M2 up to 3 m), so the page does not use it to stand for lakes.
